name: printf
description: Formats and prints data like the C printf: precise control over numbers, padding, and escapes.

flags.description: Newline / tab — printf does NOT add a newline automatically.

examples.explanation: Formats values into a template. Note the explicit \n.
Column formatting: %-10s left-pads to width 10 — quick aligned tables.
Prints each .txt filename on its own line — safer than echo for lists.

about: printf is a builtin in bash and POSIX-standard, so its behavior is identical everywhere — unlike echo. The format string is reused if there are more arguments than placeholders, which makes printf "%s\n" list a clean way to print one item per line.
mistakes: Forgetting \n and getting everything on one line.
Using %d with non-numeric input — it errors or prints 0.
